question:
(a) State the important properties of photons which support the particle nature of light.
(b) Calculate the energy of a photon of wavelength $500\,\text{nm}$. Take $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{J s}$ and $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

options.A:
(a) Photons have non-zero rest mass and zero momentum.
(b) $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=3.978\times10^{-18}\,\text{J}$.
options.B:
(a) Photon energy is independent of frequency and photons travel slower than $c$.
(b) $E=1.989\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.
options.C:
(a) Photons have $E=h\nu=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, momentum $p=\dfrac{h}{\lambda}$, zero rest mass, travel with speed $c$ in vacuum, and transfer energy in quanta.
(b) $E=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3.0\times10^8}{500\times10^{-9}}=3.978\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}\approx3.98\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.
options.D:
(a) Photons have energy $E=\dfrac{h}{\nu}$ and no momentum.
(b) $E=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\text{J}$.
